name: Land Facet Corridor Designer 3-Class Topographic Position
description: The three-class topographic position classification used to partition a landscape into canyons, slopes and ridges before clustering it into land facets (Land Facet Corridor Designer manual): RAW TPI, with cells at least 6 elevation units BELOW the neighborhood mean classed Canyons (1), at least 6 units ABOVE it Ridges (3), and everything between Slopes (2). No slope criterion, so it can be applied to a TPI raster alone. The manual's authors experimented with neighborhood sizes in three diverse landscapes and settled on a circular radius of 5 cells; the -6/+6 thresholds are elevation units of a METERS DEM, so adjust them for other units or landscapes.
source: Jenness, J., B. Brost, and P. Beier. 2013. Land Facet Corridor Designer. http://corridordesign.org (manual, Create a 3-Category Topographic Position Raster).
